item.title: Tributes paid to long-serving Longford Councillor
item.description: Tributes have been paid to long-serving Longford Councillor Seamus Finnan who passed away on Sunday. He served on Longford County Council for over 30 years from 1967 to 1999. item.title: Councillor clarifies rail remarks
item.description: A former general election candidate has clarified comments she made over the future of smaller stops on the Sligo to Dublin rail line. In December, Sligo Cllr Marie Casserly proposed options such as express services while retaining critical local access points. At this month's meeting of the Carrick-on-Shannon Municipal District meeting, representatives moved to write to Iarnród Éireann objecting to any plans that might see trains skip smaller stations. item.title: Local schools continue to send students to third-level
item.description: Two schools in the Shannonside region are topping the table when it comes to sending their students on to third level education. The Irish Independent Feeder Schools report, published this week, showed that two schools across Longford, Leitrim and Roscommon sent 100 per cent of their students on to third level education in 2025. item.title: Local TD's accused of political theatrics in the Dáil
item.description: Local TDs have been accused of political theatrics during a Dáil debate on the Mercosur Trade Deal. Minister of State Timmy Dooley was responding to a Sinn Féin motion condemning Ireland's handling of negotiations. Sligo-Leitrim TD Martin Kenny had earlier accused the Government of 'riding two horses' when it came to the deal. Independent Ireland staged a mass anti-Mercosur protest in Athlone last weekend. item.title: Local cancer patient waits 6 weeks for chemotherapy
item.description: A cancer patient from Roscommon-Galway constituency had to wait 6 weeks for chemotherapy. Sinn Féin Leader Mary-Lou McDonald raised the case in the Dáil today. She said the mother of two was diagnosed with breast cancer back in November, and has only started her treatment in the last week. item.title: Local TD backs single-use vape bill
item.description: A local TD has backed the Public Health Bill on single-use vapes. The Bill aims to ban the sale of disposable vapes to protect youth health and reduce environmental waste. Roscommon-Galway TD Martin Daly said that single-use vapes exploit a regulatory gap by combining addictive nicotine with electronic waste in a product designed to be quickly discarded. item.title: Concerns over state of CAMHS intensify
item.description: Concerns over the state of Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) in the Shannonside region have intensified. It provides assessment and treatment for young people aged under 18 who are experiencing mental health difficulties, such as depression, anxiety or dealing with an eating disorder.
